references.text: The destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah with sulfur and fire from the Lord, which is the original event referred to in Deuteronomy 29:22.
Abraham sees smoke rising from the land like smoke from a furnace, a description of the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah.
Isaiah compares Israel to Sodom and Gomorrah as an image of complete destruction.
Babylon will be like when God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah - the same language of judgment and motive for destruction.
The prophecy against Edom uses the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah as a comparison for total devastation.
The prophecy against Babylon employs the motif of Sodom and Gomorrah to describe complete destruction.
Mentions Admah and Zeboiim together with the context of destruction, the same cities mentioned in Deuteronomy 29:22.
Zephaniah prophesies that Moab and Ammon will become like Sodom and Gomorrah - a barren wasteland filled with salt and weeds.
Amos refers to God's destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah as a warning to Israel.
Jesus refers to the destruction of Sodom by fire and sulfur as an image of the coming judgment.
Peter mentions Sodom and Gomorrah, which were reduced to ashes, as an example of God's judgment on the ungodly.
Jude refers to Sodom and Gomorrah, who suffered the punishment of eternal fire, as a warning.
